patterns.name: Long dash
patterns.tip: Swap most long dashes for a period, comma or colon. Keep one per few paragraphs, only for a real interruption.

patterns.name: Spaced hyphen used as a dash
patterns.tip: A spaced hyphen is a dash in disguise. Use a period or comma.

patterns.name: Semicolon
patterns.tip: Semicolons stack up in generated drafts. Try a period.

patterns.name: Curly quotes
patterns.tip: Fine if your editor curls quotes. A flag only when the whole text was pasted unedited.

patterns.name: Several dashes in one paragraph
patterns.tip: Two dashes in one paragraph. Replace most with periods.

patterns.name: Colon reveal
patterns.tip: Write the payoff as one plain sentence.

patterns.name: Machine vocabulary cluster
patterns.tip: One is a coincidence, three in a paragraph is a signature. Use the plain word.

patterns.name: Soft machine vocabulary
patterns.tip: Often fine alone. Check whether a plainer word works.

patterns.name: Copula avoidance
patterns.pattern: serves as|serve as|stands as|stand as|acts as|functions as|represents a|marks a
patterns.tip: Use "is".

patterns.name: Marketing verbs
patterns.tip: Use "has", or describe the thing directly.

patterns.name: Vague indirect connection
patterns.pattern: in connection with|associated with|linked to|in collaboration with|in the context of
patterns.tip: Say who did what.

patterns.name: Not just X, but Y
patterns.tip: State the real claim directly. Cut the denial.

patterns.name: It's not X, it's Y
patterns.tip: Say the point once, with no setup and negate.

patterns.name: Rather than hedge
patterns.tip: If the alternative nobody raised matters, say why. Otherwise cut it.

patterns.name: I don't just X, I Y
patterns.tip: Keep the second half and attach a number.

patterns.name: Three adjectives in a row
patterns.tip: Reflex triples. Keep a three only if you counted three things.

patterns.name: Run of very short sentences
patterns.tip: Three tiny sentences in a row. Join them, or keep the one that earns a pause.

patterns.name: Question answered at once
patterns.tip: Cut the question and lead with the answer.

patterns.name: Recap closer
patterns.pattern: in conclusion|to sum up|to summarize|in summary|overall, this|all in all|to wrap up|at the end of the day|in short,
patterns.tip: Delete the recap or add one new fact.

patterns.name: Hedging phrases
patterns.pattern: can often|can be|may help|tends to|tend to|arguably|in some cases|to some extent|potentially|typically|generally speaking|it could be argued
patterns.tip: Commit to the claim and give the evidence.

patterns.name: Filler transitions
patterns.pattern: furthermore|moreover|additionally|crucially|notably|importantly|it's worth noting|it is worth noting|worth mentioning|indeed,
patterns.tip: Delete, or use "and" and "so".

patterns.name: Editorializing -ing clause
patterns.tip: Cut the clause or swap in a measured result.

patterns.name: Heading with no body
patterns.tip: Add one real sentence under every heading.

patterns.name: Claim of showing, no evidence
patterns.tip: State the evidence instead of claiming it shows something.

patterns.name: Significance inflation
patterns.pattern: testament to|(?:played|plays|play) an? (?:key|crucial|vital|pivotal|significant|major) (?:role|part)|rich tapestry|indelible|enduring legacy|shaping the future|turning point|watershed|transformative|stands as an?
patterns.tip: Name the checkable outcome.

patterns.name: Vague attribution
patterns.tip: Name the source or give the measured fact.

patterns.name: Faces-challenges, vague-optimism close
patterns.pattern: \bdespite (?:these|the|its|such|any|some)\s+(?:\w+\s+)?(?:challenges|setbacks|obstacles|limitations|hurdles)|always more to (?:build|do|learn)|where I am today|looking ahead|the future (?:looks|is) bright|excited (?:for|about) what(?:'s|’s)? next|continues to (?:evolve|grow)
patterns.tip: End on a concrete next step, or stop.

patterns.name: Chat register in a document
patterns.pattern: let's dive|let’s dive|let's explore|let's take a look|let's walk through|let's get started|let's jump in|let's look at
patterns.tip: Write as a person describing their own work.

patterns.name: Signposting
patterns.pattern: let's break this down|let's unpack|here's the thing|here's where it gets|here's what you need to know|here's the kicker|buckle up|without further ado|dive into|deep dive
patterns.tip: Just say the content.

patterns.name: Flattery before the answer
patterns.tip: Skip the praise and answer. Disagree if the facts call for it.

patterns.name: Apology hedging and sign-offs
patterns.pattern: i hope this helps|hope that helps|i apologize for|apologies for any|sorry for any confusion|let me know if you have|feel free to reach out|don't hesitate to|happy to help|i'd be happy to
patterns.tip: Cut the hedge and the sign-off. End on the last useful fact.

patterns.name: Humanizing filler sounds
patterns.tip: Do not insert filler sounds to seem human. Speak plainly.

patterns.name: Colon-led list dump
patterns.tip: Write a real sentence or a real bulleted list.

patterns.name: Heavy bold in one paragraph
patterns.tip: Bold at most one true key term per paragraph.

patterns.name: Bold-first bullets
patterns.tip: Bold only where it earns emphasis.

patterns.name: Title Case header
patterns.tip: Pick one heading style. Sentence case suits personal writing.

patterns.name: Emoji
patterns.tip: Use real bullets. Keep at most one deliberate accent.

patterns.name: Leftover chat tool artifacts
patterns.tip: Delete pasted tool debris before sending.

patterns.name: Adjective-stuffed alt text
patterns.tip: Describe what is visible, plainly.

patterns.name: Inflated diagram labels
patterns.tip: Label by what it is and does.

patterns.name: Hype adjectives
patterns.tip: Open with your job function and one proof point.

patterns.name: Corporate jargon
patterns.pattern: thought leader|thought leadership|cross-functional|disruptor|moving the needle|move the needle|at the intersection of|seamlessly integrated|best-in-class|value-add|low-hanging fruit|circle back|world-class|drive innovation
patterns.tip: Name the concrete thing the jargon stands for.

patterns.name: Slogan tagline
patterns.pattern: \bturning \w+ into \w+|\btransforming \w+ into \w+|bridging the gap between|\bwhere \w+ meets \w+
patterns.tip: Use a plain title, one or two tools, one result.

patterns.name: Closing kicker
patterns.tip: End on the last real fact.

patterns.name: Not X. Not Y. Just Z.
patterns.tip: Fold into one sentence.

judgment.name: Rule of three
judgment.question: Does every list in the piece have exactly three items?

judgment.name: Section titles echoed
judgment.question: Does any section open by repeating its own heading as the subject?

judgment.name: Uniform sentence length
judgment.question: Read aloud: do most sentences run 15 to 25 words with the same shape?

judgment.name: Structural balance
judgment.question: Does every section get about the same space, whatever its importance?

judgment.name: Parallel card copy
judgment.question: Do the cards or bullets share one grammar and one length?

judgment.name: Job-ad mirroring
judgment.question: Does any bullet echo the job posting's wording with no detail added?

judgment.name: Seamless career story
judgment.question: Does the story admit at least one gap, pivot or setback?

judgment.name: Tidy summary
judgment.question: Does the ending only restate what was already said?

judgment.name: Hedge on everything
judgment.question: Is every claim qualified, so nothing is stated flatly?

judgment.name: Facts outrank voice
judgment.question: Did the polish add any claim you have not verified?

judgment.name: Flat register
judgment.question: After cutting, is there still one opinion, one story or one joke?

judgment.name: Final read-aloud
judgment.question: Read it aloud: would a person say it this way?
